utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. And Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Barney Thomas, Bronagh McKenna, Dan Saxon, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all. Mr. Perisic is represented today by Novak Lukic and Gregor Guy-Smith as Defence counsel. Chad Mair, Boris Zorko, and our intern, Esther Brilliant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good afternoon, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Skrbic, once again and I hope for the last time in this courtroom. I'll be covering the number of topics with you that Mr. Saxon has been asking you questions about for the past two days. I will try to obtain some answers by way of clarification. On day one which was Friday, Mr. Saxon was asking a number of questions. And you spent a lot of time dealing with a topic that we might define as the informing process or information while you were still with the JNA staff, the VJ at the time. At 11880 through 11884, you spoke of the information department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My transcript for Friday goes as far as 11650. I don't know if there's a mistake in the translation or if Mr. Lukic misspoke in terms of the transcript page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have some pages that I retrieved from LiveNote the 18th and the starting page is 11850. This also ends with the following page. Just a minute, please, Your Honours. 11920. The date is the 18th of June, Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what about 11920? Oh, the following page. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last page for that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to create a problem or take anyone's time, it's simply that I have a hard copy of the transcript. My hard copy from Friday ends at page 11651, but I will try to follow from the LiveNote, Your Honour, and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to get to 11920 on LiveNote. If you can do that, maybe the person who printed it out for you didn't print all the pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, it ends with the end of Friday's session, Your Honour, what I have here, so. Let me just check one moment, please. On LiveNote from Friday the 18th, Friday's session ends at 11650.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So both of you are off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not off, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Didn't you say 11650?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, that's where I end, Your Honour, as well with my hard copy. So I'm not quite sure what Mr. Lukic is referring to here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, I'm not schooled in this technology, I still get pages 1 to 72 for the 18th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Registrar, who knows these things far better than I do, is going to try and see if he can come to your rescue. It will take something like five minutes, and do you want Mr. Lukic to wait until you are assisted, or do you feel comfortable to go on while we are waiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's carry on, Your Honour, and if I run into problems then I'll ask for more assistance. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a suggestion by Mr. Mair, the Prosecutor can follow by following only the last two digits of each of my figures and then they should be able to take that approach, they should be able to follow the whole thing or at least that's what I'm hoping. At any rate, what I'm trying to raise with Mr. Skrbic now is at pages 11880 through 11884. That's the LiveNote reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Srbic, you remember mentioning this bulletin that was produced by the information department of the JNA General Staff, it was actually the VJ at the time, which gathered information from various sources across the media. Mr. Saxon asked you whether you followed international media as well such as the BBC, International Sky News, the Reuters and so on and so forth. You do remember mentioning that, do you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, throughout 1992 and 1993 while you were still there in the General Staff of the VJ, do you know if there was a large scale media propaganda at any point in time with a view to the interests of various political structures both domestic and international?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Mr. Lukic. We called it a fierce media propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And why did you call it that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because up until that point in time, no such propaganda had ever been targeted at the JNA or the VJ. And then the media suddenly started this campaign and all the headlines filled up. Most of this was meant to target the JNA and its role, and then simply because there was a difference in terms of intensity, we now call this fierce propaganda or a large-scale propaganda campaign, and also because this was becoming a frequent occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also told Mr. Saxon that the information that was processed by the information department and in those bulletins was also in reference to the region as a whole. So what about that kind of information, referring to the region as a whole, did you see that also as something that contained a lot of propaganda or propaganda-related elements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I think that is a leading question, Your Honour. The better -- the more appropriate formulation of that question would be to ask the witness to describe the kind of information coming from the region as a whole, not to put labels out there for the witness to agree to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, subject of discussion on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm doing my best, Your Honour, to avoid leading questions. I was just picking up what I'd previously left off. I don't think that was in any way leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where did you previously leave off?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had been speaking about this media propaganda campaign in relation to the JNA, and now the witness also mentioned information in relation to the region as a whole. I'm asking him whether there was any media propaganda going on in relation to that. I think I was just following up and no more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I suppose maybe the way to ask the question without suggesting any answer is to ask him what effect this propaganda had on the region, then let him tell the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, you heard the phrasing, can you please answer.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it was easier for me to answer the previous question, whereas now, I have to be as brief as possible. I'll tell you that the effects of this propaganda was as follows: The armed forces, the JNA, and the VJ were being portrayed throughout all these events in the war news specifically, and then there were often comments being made in a negative light depending on the source. Nevertheless, throughout the SFRY and then the FRY there were hardly any positive or encouraging comments regarding those developments. Yes, there were at some point but not to the same extent. And I have to remind you as well, that at the time there was the multi-party system arising in the SFRY. And things being what they were, each of these political parties had its own vision, its own platform on how the defence effort should work, how the army should be organised. And they addressed that publicly. I'm not going into the question of whether we needed many parties or not, but the fact remains that some of them were speaking about the army in very negative terms. Another topic that they were looking at all the time was mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us about that already. But my question is as following: In your administration in the information department, you often have this influx of information, if I may call it that. What about 1992 and 1993 while you were there. How much credence did you lend to the CNN, the BBC, Sky News and so on and so forth in their reports, their reports on the region as a whole?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What I heard through the interpretation, this is page 7, line 4 Mr. Lukic said, "in your administration in the information department." It is my understanding that that is not an accurate description of what the witness told us on cross-examination that the information department came from a different administration, although I stand to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Information department came from a different administration, which administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with which administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But not the one in which he was?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Not the Administration for Morale and Information as incongruous as that may sound, Your Honour, but I stand to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I seem to remember something to that effect, yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to avoid leading at all costs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is something that has already been testified to. Mr. Skrbic told us that at that time the information department was not part of that administration of which he was a member. It was some other little department on the side. Okay, I see you shake your head. Fine, you clarify the issue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Skrbic, what was the organisational unit of which you were part in 1992 and 1993 in the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Administration for Morale and Information, which comprised three different departments; the morale department, I was part of that. The second one was the information department, and I was not involved in that, but I was in the administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And was your administration called Administration for Morale and Information or was it Morale, Information and Personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it was called the Morale and Information Administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may just return to the previous question, General, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Within your administration, the morale information administration, how much credence did you lend at the time to information obtained from foreign media and TV stations in terms of their coverage of the region?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we took a critical approach to any source of information, both domestic and international. Whenever we could, we would verify any incoming information to see if it tallied with our own reports. Every time a comment was published we would take analytical approach and study it. Sometimes the reports and comments did not quite tally with the actual reality of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Likewise, what was your view of things when you moved on to the 2nd Krajina Corps and when you started dealing with the moral religious and legal affairs in the corps? So what was your view of things at the time regarding such information as was being bandied about by the media concerning the developments in Bosnia? Did you take those at face value as being truthful or not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was assistant commander for morale, religious and legal issues in the 2nd Krajina Corps. My access to information was quite reduced. We did have an Associated Press team who were with us throughout on the ground. These people were kind enough to convey all kinds of information to us that was available to them. So we simply relied on them. Nevertheless, it was difficult for us to get the overall picture, especially not to the extent that I had been able to while I was still with the VJ.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At page 11902 in answer to one of Mr. Saxon's questions about your status, you said your status with the VJ was not changed when he moved on to the VRS, but as of 1994 you actually served with the VRS. You remember saying that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the official decision that made you a member of the VRS, you said that in chief, but we want to know about your status as an active-duty serviceman?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first official decision was the decision on appointment to the 2nd Krajina Corps as assistant commander for --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all the other microphones please be switched off while the witness is speaking, we can't hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Skrbic. Could all microphones that are not in use be switched off because the interpreters cannot hear Mr. Skrbic. Could you please repeat your answer, please, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I can, Your Honour. Do I need to move my closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you don't have to as long as all other microphones that are not in use at the time you are answering are switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat my answer. I took up my duties as assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs with the 2nd Krajina Corps of the VRS, pursuant to a decision by the defence minister of the Republika Srpska. And the other decision was a decree by the president of the Republika Srpska on my appointment to the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P191, which is the Law on the Military of Republika Srpska. And could we zoom in on Article 2 which is at the very beginning of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, while you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, were you familiar with the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please turn his microphone off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 2 says in paragraph 1: "Military service in the army shall include military and other duties in the active and reserve forces in time of peace and war time." And then paragraph 2 goes on to say who members of the members of active strength and who are of the reserve strength. From the moment you joined the Army of Republika Srpska which category of servicemen did you fall into?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fell into the category of the permanent staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the following article, please: Article 3. Can we scroll up the page a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This article defines the category of active duty servicemen and Article 3 says: "The persons serving in the army are soldiers, active members of the military reserve personnel and non-commissioned officers." From the moment you joined the Army of Republika Srpska, Mr. Skrbic, what was your status and what did that status arise from, from which legal act, from which law?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I was an active serviceman pursuant to the law that we have on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now can we move on to Article 4. I will invite some comments from the witness. Article 4 speaks about the relations in the service, let me not quote the article for you because I believe that you are very familiar with it without -- even without me reading it. I'm going to wait for the page to be moved a little and zoomed in on Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The B/C/S is no longer there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is still there, I see Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, we don't see the bottom part. We have to move the document to the left just a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were a member of the 2nd Krajina Corps, General Skrbic, who was your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Grujo Boric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was his superior?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His superior was the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was his superior pursuant to this law?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His superior was the supreme commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, president of Republika Srpska, Mr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, did General Perisic or anybody else from the Army of Yugoslavia ever issue orders to you, were any of them in a position to issue orders to you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 2nd Krajina Corps I reported to the corps commander. In the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska to the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it comes to General Perisic or any other from the Army of Yugoslavia, were they in a position to convey their authorities to anybody in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Lukic, what you don't have you cannot transfer or convey on to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did General Perisic or anybody else from the Army of Yugoslavia have the authority to instigate any disciplinary proceedings against you for any actions that you may have committed while you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not even the commander of the Main Staff was allowed to do that in the Army of Republika Srpska let alone General Perisic. It is up to the judiciary bodies to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose judiciary bodies?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The judiciary bodies of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was in a position to appoint you to any duty while you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska? You don't have to give me any names, just tell me their army affiliation.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I've already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agree. Let's not repeat ourselves, you are absolutely right. Let's talk about something else that was subject of the cross-examination yesterday on page 11909.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday on page 17 of yesterday's LiveNote, I don't have the exact page number from the transcript, however, Mr. Skrbic, you will remember that Mr. Saxon asked you some questions and showed you some documents referring to a period when Yugoslavia imposed sanctions on Republika Srpska and he showed you that even when those sanctions were in place, the Army of Yugoslavia still continued to assist the Army of Republika Srpska. There was a document about some shells, a document signed by General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember all those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, during that year and a half or rather, from the moment you joined the General Staff in the month of August when sanctions were imposed until 1995 or the end of the war, where was your command post? Where were you stationed? Where was your rear command post?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear command post where my sector was also deployed was in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which other sector shared the same premises with you, can you remind us?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logistics, and later on the sector for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And during the year and a half while you were there up until the end of the war, did you often see General Djukic and the chief of the logistics sector?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you this: From the moment the sanctions were imposed, what information was conveyed to you by General Djukic and your colleagues from the logistics department about the sanctions imposed by the state of Yugoslavia, were the sanctions strict or were they violated?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic and I never discussed the issue of sanctions with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the sessions of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and if you did, did General Djukic read reports to the [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at the time when Yugoslavia imposed sanctions on Republika Srpska, whether General Djukic mentioned any problems with regard to the procurement of goods for the Army of Republika Srpska from the Army of Yugoslavia? Did he say that there were problems or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We now have a compound question that is effectively a leading question. The simplest question would be what, if anything, the witness recalls from the reports of General Djukic and then we can move on from there, step by step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems I can't have it both ways, be quick and still comply with the procedure. If I'm to take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let me tell you something. If you take it step by step, you might sound like you are asking many questions but because you are asking very short questions, very focused questions you will get very short and focused answer and you will move faster through the thing. If you ask compound questions, you are taking more time because you were inviting these kind of objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about General Djukic, at these briefings at the Main Staff, did he inform the members of the Main Staff on the logistics situation that prevailed in the VRS at a given point in time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Nevertheless, Mr. Lukic, I would like to ask you to not head into something that I'm perhaps not up to discussing. I wasn't following at the time, nor was I in the habit of remembering specific details. It just wasn't my field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's move on, please. Likewise, Mr. Saxon asked you about this group of officers in July 1995 who came to the VRS, Bogdan Sladojevic, Trkulja, Stankovic, those men, you do remember, don't you? When they arrived in Han Pijesak, where were they first deployed?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that. Which officers? Trkulja was with the Main Staff, Sladojevic Bogdan was deployed to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the question was about him and then Trkulja was later with that group?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with the Main Staff of the VRS. He was head of anti-armour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before Sladojevic arrived in Han Pijesak did he know already what his first deployment would be, had anyone told him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This question is asking the witness to speculate as to what was inside the head of Bogdan Sladojevic. I don't think that's a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think that objection would be overruled, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So my question, do you know whether Sladojevic had been told before he arrived in Han Pijesak about what his deployment would be?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As in you don't know?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not know where his deployment would be. Like question like answer, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who told him that he would be deployed to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps when he arrived in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Colonel Malcic. He just conveyed the information. But the decision had been previously taken by the Main Staff. Bukamik Maltic [phoen] was the mediator here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who made the decision for him to be deployed to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS Main Staff commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who had the power to change that decision?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He alone. When I say "he" I mean the VRS Main Staff commander again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were asked by Mr. Saxon whether you knew about Sladojevic, Trkulja, Stankovic, at one point in time in those days appearing in the Drina Corps area, you said you had read about that in Richard Butler's expert report, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, Mr. Lukic. I did say that and that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about you as head of the organisation mobilisation and system related affairs sector at the time? Did you know at the time, would you have known that instead of being sent to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps he was sent to the area covered by the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those were daily orders and commands. I wasn't in charge of that or indeed even knowing about that and I wasn't informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this an effective appointment to a post, or is it just a daily assignment, a task? Can you please elaborate because I fail to understand the distinction.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan Sladojevic was appointed to the Main Staff of the VRS. He was subordinated to General Radivoje Miletic or at least that's what I think. He was given a task by his superior and the task was to go there, and perhaps he was ordered directly and personally by the commander of the VRS Main Staff, but that is not for me to speculate about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on to a different topic. Mr. Saxon was showing you certain documents yesterday, in a bit to put it to you that the Army of Yugoslavia could just call directly on certain officers from the VRS for them to go back to the Army of Yugoslavia, do you remember that? Tihomir Babic specifically was a case in point.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you again, firstly, from the moment you arrived at the Main Staff, could a single officer of the VRS leave the VRS without object obtaining approval from General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were with the 2nd Krajina Corps did the same rules apply?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time there, the same rules applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You answered Mr. Saxon that you had certain reservations regarding certain actions taken by the personnel officer in the Drina Corps, Jovicic, and your reservations had do with the form of the documents that he produced. That was at page 36 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. We are in open session nevertheless, so I would kindly ask you to spare me any comments that I would have to make regarding that man's personality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, that wasn't my intention at all, I was just trying to follow up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2568, please. Can we have that brought up next, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are waiting for P2568, Mr. Lukic just asked you if anybody from -- where is it? Yes, that the Army of Yugoslavia could just call certain officers from the VRS to come back to the Army of Yugoslavia. He said "could." My question is, did it ever do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not certain about the specific sections, but the general answer would be no they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, do you know of any officer or soldier who left the VRS of his own or her own accord and went back to the VJ? Do you know of anybody who did do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were several.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But just left on their own without being called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, if I may, we are in open session, and it's difficult for me to name any names, but you should understand if I tell you that we referred to them as deserters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we in open session? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you can actually see the document clearly, General, the copy is somewhat poor.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it is, but I can still see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You signed this document, didn't you, as far as I can see?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment about the format of this document in the light of my previous question?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure about the second sentence, I am not sure that I can read what it says, but I do have an inference about what it probably says. The gist of the document is me informing the 30th KC not to approve the request submitted by Milorad Popovic. Is that right, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm reading it too.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked whether that was my signature; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about this document, would that be part of one's personal file with the 30th Personnel Centre or the VJ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You analysed the personnel file of Vujadin Popovic yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have that back, P1934, that is service mobility, Vujadin Popovic personnel file, page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure either. No, I'm being told no. The English page is ERN 0422-8609. The B/C/S reference is page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You remember seeing this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to focus on, this is where it says that he was chief of the security department in the organ for intelligence and security affairs. The 30th Personnel Centre. Can you see that? And then Judge Moloto asked you how we could ascertain whether he was really at the time member of the VJ or the Army of -- or the VRS. You remember that; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I just look at the date here. When did his appointment take effect, the one mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the security affairs department within the security administration, the 15th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry. I want to know about this entry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before the witness responds, Your Honour, I have to at least make an objection. Page 25, lines 21 to 22 in -- Mr. Lukic says: "And then Judge Moloto asked you how we could ascertain whether he was really at the time member of the VJ or the VRS." Mr. Lukic hasn't cited any page number, but the page number that I'm looking at from yesterday is page 11967 of the transcript, and Judge Moloto begins to speak on line 12, and around line 17, Judge Moloto says: "And then when you talk of a transfer to the -- to head security administration, okay, this one says 30th Personnel Centre, if he goes back, is he going back to the VJ, or is he still in the VRS?" And well, this is what I find in the transcript which is different from the comment or question formulated today by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I phrased the question based on what I had read in the transcript at page 45 of yesterday's LiveNote, line 19. The words of Judge Moloto where he says: [In English] "How do we determine, in fact, that this person is going back to the VJ when in fact certain post in the VRS are described as V post Belgrade 30th Personnel Centre when in fact we know that the person is in the VRS. How do we determine without a narration that this is the real transfer or maybe just of an intention of it?"

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to interpret your words as they are in the transcript, but I interpreted your words, and I'm looking now where Mr. Lukic is reading from as referring to whether a person is physically in the VRS and then physically going to a position in the VJ, which is the concern of this part of Vujadin Popovic's personnel file. Mr. Lukic's question referred to membership in the armies, and that is a different intellectual concept, Your Honour. That's what I'm getting at. Because obviously it is the Prosecution's position that membership was retained in the VJ while these gentleman were serving in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My understanding of your concern, Your Honour, my understanding of your question was -- I apologise to the interpreters. My understanding of your question was like this: How and whether based on this entry we could determine whether he was a member of the VRS or a member of the VJ. Perhaps I was the one who misinterpreted your question. If so, please accept my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your apology is accepted, but I don't know whether the parties want me to explain myself. Obviously if you -- my concern was where the person physically is, first of all. Then, of course, whether the document that has been put on the screen does not only tell us exactly where he is physically, but it also gives us the status of that person and the membership of that person to a particular army, but the membership is really not important here because we have heard evidence of confusion between -- on the membership of the different armies, but just where that person is physically following an order given. If you give an order, you say, I transfer you from the VRS to the VJ 30th Personnel Centre. Now, I know that when you were in the VRS, you were already at 30th Personnel Centre, but then when you say you are transferring me back there, am I really getting back there, or am I still in the VRS and in the Republika Srpska. It doesn't -- without a narration, it is very difficult given what was going on at the time to determine whether this is an actual movement of the person from the Republika Srpska back to Belgrade to be in the personnel -- 30th Personnel Centre, or no, no, no, we just putting you in the personnel centre but you are still in the Republika Srpska because the important thing for purposes of the trial, as I understand it, is to know where a person was physically, so that if that person committed a crime, for which we have to deal with here, obviously if he was fictitiously there, not in reality, then he didn't commit that crime. But if he was there in reality, then he did commit that crime. So it is exactly the physical presence of the person that we want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Things are much clearer to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that what you wanted to ask General Skrbic is this: General, on the 30th of September, 1998, which is the date of the document, does the document show where Vujadin Popovic was as of that moment physically, whether he was in the VJ or in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are talking about an order issued by the personnel department 170/59. I apologise, I just touched the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an order, it doesn't say much. The date that matters is the 15th of September, 1998, however, even based on that date, you could not conclude anything as to his physical whereabouts, and this is where the Trial Chamber and His Honour are right. This only regulates his status as of the 15th of September, 1998. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was there security administration of the 30th Personnel Centre in the VJ? Was there such an administration in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, please, Mr. Lukic, don't take me back to the things that I've already explained very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could the Court please produce a document belonging to the financial file of Mr. Vujadin Popovic. It is on 65 ter list of the OTP under 7322. Could we see at the document, doc ID 1D12/435. Let's just retain the date that you mentioned, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Lukic. You are giving us an OTP 65 ter list number. Are you not able to give us the -- is this a new document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a new document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have it on your 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why don't you give us your 65 ter list number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have not given any documents any particular numbers. Documents that already bear 65 ter number from the OTP we just transfer them on to our list. We didn't want to confuse the matter with new 65 ter numbers. That was our agreement with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If that was the agreement, at least you have clarified that. Mr. Registrar, are you able to identify that document and find it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is Defence 65 ter document under number 3365D. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought they said they didn't have that document number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 20 October 1998. I believe that the document is self-explanatory. However, maybe you can tell us about VP 7572 Bijeljina. Which army did this military post belong to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This what was a military post belonging to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the Court also produce another document from the same financial file of Mr. Vujadin Popovic. Doc ID is 1D12/0433.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we go to that document, what do you want to do with this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D354. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can it be marked for identification pending an official translation because what we have now is just a draft translation made by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the same financial file, doc ID 1D12/0433. We are still on the financial file for Mr. Popovic. We marked this document as 65 ter 3364D and as I said, it is part of that same 65 ter document by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a certificate from the same military post that Mr. Vujadin Popovic had addressed in the previous document. Can you please look at the stamp and the signature and could you please tell us which army did they belong to? Which military?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp is of the Army of Republika Srpska, the military post in Bijeljina, and it was signed by Major-General Dragisa Masal who was my successor in the General Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this document on the 22nd October 1998, which military did Vujadin Popovic belong to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that he was a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D355. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is the translation correct and it doesn't need to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I've just been informed, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I asked you a question. Is this official translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. It's not. I apologise, I apologise. It is not an official translation so the document needs to the MFI'd. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can it be marked for identification, please. And, Mr. Lukic, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday on page 57 of the LiveNote, Mr. Saxon asked you about the period while you were standing in between 1997 and 2000 in the personnel administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown one part of his financial file, which is also a document from the Defence 65 ter list which was previously a Prosecutor 65 ter document under 7389, page 62, doc ID 1D12/0424.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is an order on standing in sent to the accountancy service and under the stamp, I believe that I can read the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How do you see that it was sent to the accountancy service? Well, I apologise, I can see it now myself. I apologise. This is -- oh, rather, yesterday, when we were looking at the excerpt of documentation about your career, does this document have anything to do with that one that we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have not seen this document before. The person, whoever he is, does not receive this document. This document is sent only to the accountancy service, nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now what I can read here is this: Petar Skrbic, and underneath the Belgrade Garrison, Skrbic, Petar, currently the assistant Chief of the General Staff of the 30th Personnel Centre for recruitment, mobilisation, and legal affairs, FC, which is your establishment rank and so on and so forth, how do you explain this? At the moment when those documents was issued which was on the 13th January, 1997, were you still in the position of the assistant Chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, if I can put it that way, for recruitment, mobilisation, and legal affairs?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are only elements that regulated my pay, and they had to be taken into account by the accountancy service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why was it then necessary to write this in order for the accountancy service to pay you your salary, your remuneration?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, I would like to draw your attention to the wording. FC stands for the establishment rank, major-general. Another FC, major-general, and the position group 5. All these are elements that constitute the remuneration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this document, your regular duty was to be the assistant chief of the 30th Personnel Centre and in addition to that, you were standing in at the vacant post of the assistant chief of the personnel administration for the 30th Personnel Centre. That's how I am reading this document; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are. That's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let's now look at another thing, the following sentence reads: "He will be standing in for the chief in addition to his regular duties."

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's go back to something that I asked you on the examination-in-chief and something that you also discussed with Mr. Saxon. First, on page 11808, you told me, and then you confirmed it yesterday on page 57 when Mr. Saxon gave you his references, you said that you were not duty-bound to come to work regularly while you were standing in for somebody else. Do you remember that that is what you said?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then on page 61, you confirmed to Mr. Saxon that during that period of time, you were duty-bound to come to work. Can you please clarify and can you please tell us whether from January 1997 up to 2000 when you were again re-assigned to duty in the VJ, were you duty-bound to come to work every day?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody did things erroneously. Either you or the transcript is wrong, I don't know. I can only tell you what I said. I said that I wasn't duty-bound to come to work every day but I did nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any of the VRS generals whose duty in the VRS was discontinued and who was placed at the disposal of the Army of Yugoslavia, did any of them like you did come to work every day, were they duty-bound to come to work at the Army of Yugoslavia up to the moment when they were pensioned off?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody but me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be given an exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could it also please be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D356 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon also showed you a certain number of documents with your personal appraisal that are now in the personnel files. You remember that there were two personnel appraisal forms that were shown to you. I believe that Mr. Saxon will remember and understand my question even without me referring to the exact page numbers. Do you remember all that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the rules, who was who provided a personnel appraisal or evaluation about a certain person if that evaluation covers a period of three years during which that person changed positions, posts, and duties? Who is it who is duty-bound to provide that person's evaluation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One's immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit P1953 on our screens. 1953.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is that we see here?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official assessment. Shall I tell you who it refers to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And for which period?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official assessment for [indiscernible] Captain Ljubisa Beara for the period from 10 December 1990 to 10 December 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can one see from this document when this assessment was conveyed to Mr. Beara, and can you see from the signature who was it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move forward one page in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps one more page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you tell me who made this assessment, from which army, and when was this assessment conveyed to Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was conveyed to this individual on the 20th October 1995, and he confirmed that with his signature, and the assessment was made by his immediate superior, that is to say, the chief for intelligence and security, Major-General Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 20th or 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry if I said 20th. It is the 24th of October, 1995, the date when this assessment was conveyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose stamp this is, and can you tell us Zdravko Tolimir, to which army did he belong?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a so-called establishment stamp of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove this document and then can we please now have P1788. I don't think we have the correct page in English. It's all right. This will suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, only when this assessment was conveyed to Zdravko Tolimir, that's what we saw on page 1, and who made the assessment, the member of which army?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment was conveyed to this individual as far as I can see on the 4th of July, 1994. It's not quite clear. And while it could be 10th, but it's definitely July 1994, and it was signed by General Tolimir as confirmation that he was given the assessment, and the assessor was his immediate superior, the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. Shall I read the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite clear. It says General -- Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did this assessment have any effect on one's salary?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document P2021.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not quite clear, but this document stems from the Main Staff. You can see that in the left-hand top corner, which army is in question.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see but not quite clearly that this is the General Staff of the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the bottom of the page where there's the signature and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can Mr. Lukic -- this does not appear to be some kind of assessment, and so I'm struggling to understand how this particular document arises out of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to put one question, and that is, can one see from this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, just a second, Mr. Lukic. There is an objection on the floor so you don't go ahead and say no, I'll just put this -- put one question and the question is this. Answer the objection first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will. That was exactly what I was going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you are putting the question that you say you want to put, you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to continue with this topic relating to performance assessment and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, let me quote what you said, "I just want to put one question and that is, can one see from this document --" you are already going on to ask the question. Now, I'm stopping you because there is an objection. I'm saying deal with the objection before you put your question. That's all I'm saying. Deal with the objection, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Saxon asked a few questions relating to assessments and who assessed the performance of Mr. Skrbic in particular. And with this document, I want to ask an additional question relating to the process of performance assessment of military officers, and I can get this answer on the basis of this document. So this is within the scope of the topic that Mr. Saxon addressed with this issue -- this with witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't heard the question yet obviously, but this document does not appear to be an assessment, so I'm still at a loss to understand how the use of this document arises out of my cross-examination. If there is a simple question that Mr. Lukic can ask, fine, but what does this document have to do with my questions about related -- pertaining to the assessments of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is the problem. The problem is that you are objecting to the production of the document. Mr. Lukic is telling us about the question he wants to put to the witness. Now, either you suspend your objection and hear the question and see whether it's objectionable or not, or you insist on the relevance of this document before the question is put, which would be the proper procedural step to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would insist on the relevance of this document before the question is put, Your Honour. The relevance of this document to my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can say is to repeat that this document is relevant because it is connected with the topic raised by Mr. Saxon which is assessment. Regardless of the title of the document, this does not mean that it goes beyond the scope of the questions that Mr. Saxon asked, and his questions pertained to the process of performance assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not only focusing on the title of the document. I'm focusing on what I can see as to be the contents of the document, and I see nothing here that appears to me to be someone's performance assessment. Mr. Lukic can correct me if I'm reading the document incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not even sure whether I'm seeing the entire document in the English that is being shown in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me to ask the question, then I'm in your hands and you will decide whether to overrule it or reject it or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Saxon insists on you showing the relevance of the document before you put the question, and if you are not able to show the relevance of the document, then unfortunately, we can't allow the question to be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you would either have to ask the witness to leave the courtroom or the entire document to be shown to you because you can't see the relevance. If we can have the witness out of the courtroom, then I can explain to you my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be easier just then to -- if there is more to the document than I can see in English here, please show me the next page of the document. We might be able to clear this up very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would have thought so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document has one page only, and I agree -- just bear with me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised that it actually has three pages, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I'm sorry, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see -- if you can scroll down a little bit, please. The English. That's right. That very first entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I now withdraw my objection, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. See, Mr. Lukic. You may proceed now, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, from this document can we see when Ratko Mladic was assessed last time and by whom?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that. His last assessment was made on the 10th of January 1995. It has been signed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do you see that in the English, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go forward one page, please. Maybe one more page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, on the 10th of January, 1995, who was General Mladic's superior?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His superior was Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, that is to say, the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Skrbic, in view of this period between 1997 and 2000 when you were appointed as a stand-in for the 30th Personnel Centre administration -- personnel administration of the General Staff, do you know whether in that particular period any assessment of any general was made whose service was terminated in the VRS and who were placed at the disposal of the VJ? We saw your example and you testified about that in response to Mr. Saxon's questions.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such generals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished with this document and I have just a couple more questions before I finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you provided facts relating to the activities of people who were attending schooling during NATO bombing in the VJ. Can you tell me, according to what you know, how many people were actively involved in the war against NATO? And I'm talking about the persons who were attending training and schooling at the time.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I told you the exact figure. There were 30 of them in the staff school and ten of them in the national defence school. Only Miro Skoric who had a prosthesis was not assigned to any task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to these people before they departed? Did you have any direct contact with them?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they were willing to go to the war theatre in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection. Objection, that is an absolutely leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a slightly aggressive reaction, if I might say, by Mr. Saxon which will lead me to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is an aggressively leading question, too. You are going to the very heart of the issue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you talked to General Talic. You said that at page --

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no need to quote the page, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 70. Which was the position of General Talic during the NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you need to speak to him at the time? What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was he who called me, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about what I said yesterday. The deployment of the attendees of both schools, which I mentioned before, across the territory of Serbia and Montenegro during the NATO air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While Mr. Lukic is paging through, you said you talked to each one of these people who were attending the schools and the military academy, what was their reaction to their deployment to the war zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, only Major Strugar asked if we could stay for another two days. His daughter had high blood sugar at the time, or rather, had diabetes, and then I told him, yes, stick around for another two days and then report back to me. No one else asked any questions whatsoever, they got on to that bus and were off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Rather, maybe after two days, what was Mr. Strugar's reaction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He reported back and was eventually deployed. I can't remember where to though. It was in the VJ, that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At page 70, you say you talked to General Talic and he said at line 9, those who do not want to go to war should not even return here once they are finished with their education. Did you convey to them General Talic's position?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Mr. Skrbic, thank you very much. This completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Judge? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Skrbic, I have a few questions for you. Excuse me if I did not understand all the questions -- the answers you provided to the numerous questions that were put to you. First question, you are retired from what army?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I retired in the VJ, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, you never received any retirement pension from the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why not, by the way? How is it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, my status was always regulated within the VJ. At the very end I worked with the federal defence ministry and that was where my service was terminated. The FRY defence ministry, federal defence ministry. That was where I retired from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can understand that, but admittedly you could receive part of your pension from the VJ and the rest from the VRS depending on the number of years you served in one or the other army.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but unfortunately, that is not the case. Those from the VRS gave us nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true, it can be understood in war time, but now that the war is over and Bosnia has its own resources, it's rather difficult to understand that situation.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I too find it difficult to understand. I did overhear something about them paying certain forms of compensation in terms of pension in the VRS. Nevertheless, I never applied for these supplements myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question regarding your work before you started serving in the VRS. So you collected a whole series of newspaper articles, you were doing some kind of press review, but destined to whom?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Secretary For All People's Defence. That was during the SFRY. And the defence minister during the FRY, as well as all the chiefs in the General Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on you stated that one of the problems you had with the local or international press was that the information was not reliable and that there may have been a pinch of propaganda in the information, that's how I understood what you said. But you -- how did you know that the information you were receiving was not good?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: News would be compared to the actual events. We didn't ascertain that in relation to every single piece of news. We did in relation to some specific ones though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, you would receive reports from other sources?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What kind of sources were they? Were they journalists from Belgrade or was that military sources?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. When Serbia decided on an embargo on the Republic of Bosnia in August 1994, that was then, wasn't it, how long did it last roughly?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the point of view of my men, the men that I was in charge of, it went on for five months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for five months, the pay was not paid?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But did you keep receiving ammunition, military equipment, petrol?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you are bound to know that. Don't tell me you don't know that.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was reckoning they blocked everything about the personnel so there wouldn't be anything else happening, would there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Well, I find it hard to believe that you only knew about what was happening within your own department. But let's speak about it, your own department. So you were the head of the department, the personnel department in the VRS, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the personnel policy sector. That's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sector, yes. During the events in July 1995 in Srebrenica, you were based in Han Pijesak, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I guess you heard about what had happened in Srebrenica rather quickly, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I should -- I'm not saying it's an objection. It's a comment. I think we should ask the witness to leave. Your Honours, this is about what we said before the witness made his appearance. If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, sorry about that. That's what often happens in these situations. Do you think you can step out for two minutes, please, and we'll call you just now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just say one thing before I leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the answer to Madam Judge's question, it is actually contained in my two statements. The statement to Mr. McCloskey dated the 5th of May, 1995, the investigation stage. And my statement to Mr. Nicholls in September 2007 during the actual evidence that I gave. If that can be of any use whatsoever to you. As long as that is understood, I would now like to leave the courtroom as ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much. We don't have those statements, so just give us a few moments, we'll call you back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before this evidence, Your Honours, we discussed the position or status of Mr. Skrbic, in the OTP his status as a suspect. I'm here to defend the interest of my own client Mr. Perisic, and I'm in no way authorised in any way to interfere with this. I don't know, Your Honours, why he is a suspect. The OTP refuse to say. But before Judge Picard's question, I thought it might be a good idea to ask you to caution Mr. Skrbic about his rights.
